I understand the context and all of the events that have occurred up to this point. I also saw firsthand how Reddit's administrative bureaucracy repeatedly failed the community over the last several years. What I'm not sure about is how anything changes from everyone flocking to Voat. Sure, Voat in its current state does not practice censorship. Neither did Reddit's alpha version. And I'm sure Digg in its early stages didn't either. Voat cannot afford to pull any bullshit right now because it is so young and small. But what happens when they have a user base 10 million strong? 20 million? 36 million (Reddit's user base as of June 2015)? A lot of the same issues that plague Reddit today is not a reflection of the site specifically or even Ellen Pao, who has only been CEO since November 2014. A lot of these issues are endemic to what happens to a rapidly growing forum, and I just don't see how it's possible to avoid them if the people in charge want any semblance of profitability.
